title: MITK MxN Multi-Widget Layout (v2.0)
description:
Canonical layout description for QmitkMxNMultiWidgetEditor. The on-disk format of `mxnLayout_*.json` preset files and the document consumed by `QmitkMxNMultiWidget::ApplyLayout` / produced by `QmitkMxNMultiWidget::SerializeLayout`. Layout describes only the splitter tree, per-window placement state (view direction, synchronization links), and per-group state. It does NOT describe global rendering state (selected position, time, camera).

Window names: each window's `name` MUST be unique within the document. The C++ loader enforces uniqueness at apply time. The recommended default form for tool-generated layouts is `widget<i>` where `<i>` is the leaf's pre-order traversal index (0-based, no gaps). Hand-authored presets MAY use any unique, URL-segment-safe string.

Synchronization model: cells declare per-dimension links via `links.<dim>: <groupName>`. Cells with the same value for the same dimension are mutually linked and share that dimension's runtime bundle. The same group name MAY be used across multiple dimensions (e.g. `links: { selection: "main", zoom: "main" }`) — group names live in a single namespace, dimensions are orthogonal. Per-group persisted state lives in the top-level `groups` dict. v2.0 knows one such property: `select_all` (the selection bundle's UX-mode). Future v3.0 dimensions that need per-group state add their properties to the same group entry additively.

Lazy vs. strict mode: the top-level `groups` dict is OPTIONAL. When present, it is authoritative — every label appearing in any cell's `links` MUST be a key in `groups`; otherwise the loader throws (catches typos and tool-output drift). When absent, every label referenced becomes an implicit group with property defaults (`select_all: true`). Tool-generated documents SHOULD always include `groups` explicitly with every property spelled out — round-trip stability and reviewer clarity outweigh the few bytes saved by omission. Treat omission as ergonomic shorthand for human authors, not a stylistic choice for machines.

Schema is closed (`additionalProperties: false` everywhere, including inside `links` and inside group entries). v2.0 only knows the `selection` synchronization dimension and the `select_all` group property. A future v3.0 schema will add further dimensions inside `links` and possibly further properties inside group entries, with a deliberate version bump — older loaders will refuse v3.0 documents loudly at the version check. The C++ loader does not run a JSON-schema validator, so `additionalProperties: false` enforces closure only for consumers that validate the document against this schema; the loader's own defence is the explicit version check plus per-field type validation in `PrewalkValidate`.

version.description: Schema version. New documents MUST be "2.0". The C++ loader rejects any other version; writers MUST emit "2.0".

name.description: Optional human-readable preset name. Pure metadata - does not affect loading or rendering.

groups.description:
Synchronization groups referenced by cells via `links.<dim>`. Optional. When present, authoritative — every label appearing in any cell's `links` MUST be a key here; missing labels throw at load time. When absent, every referenced label becomes an implicit group with property defaults. Tool-generated documents SHOULD always include this field.

Group seeding at load: when a layout is applied, each group's runtime synchronized state for per-renderer node properties (today: per-node `visible`, per-node `layer`; future v3 keys analogously) is seeded from the cell that appears first in document order whose `links.<dim>` names that group. After seeding, every other group member is normalised to the seed cell's values for those keys. Group-scoped persisted properties stored in this top-level `groups` dict (e.g. `select_all`) are not seeded from cells — the value declared here wins outright. Selection-list membership is a runtime concept (not encoded in the layout) and is seeded from the data storage's non-helper / non-hidden nodes. Hand-authors who want a specific cell to be the seed should list that cell first among the group's members in the layout document. Document order = pre-order traversal of the splitter tree (splits' `children` arrays in array order).

root.description: Root of the layout tree. Always a split, even for a single-window layout (which is a split with one window child).

groups.description: Map from group name to group entry. Group names are arbitrary URL-segment-safe identifiers; the same name MAY be referenced from multiple dimensions in cells' `links`.

group_entry.description: Properties shared across cells linked to this group. v2.0 knows one property (`select_all`, the selection bundle's UX-mode). Future v3.0 dimensions that need per-group persisted state add their own properties here additively. Schema is closed — unknown properties are rejected.

select_all.description: Whether cells in this group display all data nodes (true) or a curated subset (false). Persisted state for the selection bundle's UX-mode. Cells linked to this group via `links.selection` share this setting at runtime. Optional; defaults to true. Has no effect if no cell references this group via `links.selection` (in which case the property is dormant).

node.description: A layout-tree node. Either an interior split or a leaf window.

split.description: An interior splitter dividing its area among children along one axis. Maps to QSplitter.

orientation.description: "horizontal" arranges children left-to-right (Qt::Horizontal); "vertical" arranges children top-to-bottom (Qt::Vertical).

size.description: Splitter weight assigned by this node's parent. Optional inside another split's `children` (default weight 1 applies when omitted); absent on the document root (which has no parent).

children.description: Ordered list of child nodes. `size` is optional on each child; omitted children take the default weight 1. Mixed siblings compute as ratios, e.g. `[size: 3, default, default]` yields 3:1:1.

window.description: A leaf render-window. Maps to QmitkRenderWindowWidget.

name.description: Window identity. The same string is used as the engine-side render-window bare name (qualified at load time as '<editorName>.<name>'). The schema enforces only URL-segment safety (alphanumeric, underscore, dot, hyphen); structural uniqueness across the document is enforced by the C++ loader at apply time. Recommended default for tool-generated layouts is "widget<i>" where <i> is the leaf's pre-order traversal index (0-based, no gaps); custom names are accepted as long as they are unique within the document.

view_direction.description: Anatomical plane shown in this window. Lowercase, matching the rest of the rendering REST surface (e.g. StdMulti window names, `/slice` plane field). "original" preserves the data's native orientation.

links.description: Per-dimension synchronization links for this window. Required: every window MUST declare `links.selection` explicitly (no implicit singletons). Tool-generated documents emit every link explicitly.

size.description: Splitter weight assigned by this window's parent split. Optional; default weight 1 applies when omitted.

links.description: Per-dimension synchronization links. Each value is a group name (string). Cells with the same value for the same dimension are mutually linked. The same group name MAY be referenced across multiple dimensions. v2.0 knows only the `selection` dimension; v3.0 will add further dimensions (zoom, time, crosshair, ...) here additively, referring to the same `groups` dict.

selection.description: Group name for the selection bundle (selection list, stack order, visibility, select_all). Cells with the same value form an implicit group; their selection state is synchronized at runtime. The named group's persisted properties live in the top-level `groups` dict if it is declared; otherwise property defaults apply. See the top-level `groups` description for the load-time seeding rule that determines which cell's per-renderer values are authoritative when group members diverge.

size.description: Splitter-child weight. Only the ratio between siblings matters; Qt redistributes weights proportionally on resize. Absolute values are NOT pixel measurements - prefer small numbers (e.g. 1, 2, 3) over screenshot-derived pixel counts. Optional; defaults to 1 when omitted, so `[size: 3, default, default]` yields a 3:1:1 split. Must be >= 1: 0 would collapse the pane in Qt, but the format has no documented 'hide this cell' semantics, so 0 is rejected by both the schema and the C++ loader.
